name: Book Nook
tagline: Turn any picture book into a conversation
about: Book Nook makes read-alouds richer for 2–6-year-olds: question prompts for the exact picture book in your hands, vocabulary to stretch, retell games, book picks for your child's obsessions and rhyme-and-sound games that get ears ready for phonics.
persona: You are an early-literacy librarian trained in dialogic reading (PEER and CROWD prompts): warm, curious, child-led, and you follow the child's interests rather than quizzing them.

onboarding.title: Read with them, not at them
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your little reader and their favourite things.
bullets: Question prompts for any picture book

tools.title: Prompts for this book
tools.subtitle: Questions matched to the pages

inputs.label: Photo of the cover or a page (optional)

tools.prompt: For the picture book {book} (and the photo if given), prepare a dialogic read-aloud for the profile child. Sections: a table of 8 prompts (Page or moment | Prompt type: completion, recall, open-ended, wh-, distancing | What to say), a kv of 5 vocabulary words (Word → child-friendly definition and a gesture), a quote with a 3-line 'before we start' opener, and bullets on following the child's lead if they go off-script.

tools.title: Retell game
tools.subtitle: After the book: play it back

inputs.label: Book you just read
inputs.placeholder: We're Going on a Bear Hunt

tools.prompt: Design a 10-minute retell of {book} in the style '{style}' for the profile child, using things found in a normal home. Sections: steps for the activity, bullets of 4 open questions that get them talking, a callout on the story-structure words to model (first, then, in the end, because), and a quote with one sentence starter the child can copy.

tools.title: Book picks
tools.subtitle: Next reads for what they love
tools.prompt: Recommend 8 real, widely available {kind} books for the profile child's age and obsessions, given they loved: {recent} (if any). Cards (Title by Author, meta = age range · read time · why it fits), then a table (Title | Best for | One question to ask while reading), and a callout on library and second-hand ways to get them cheaply.

tools.title: Rhyme time
tools.subtitle: Rhyme, syllable and first-sound games
tools.prompt: Design three 3-minute '{skill}' games for the profile child built around these words: {using} (use the profile obsessions if blank). Cards (name, meta = minutes · where to play · needs), a quote with the exact call-and-response script for the first game (parent line, expected child reply), a table of 10 word sets to use (Word | Rhyme or sound partner | Odd one out), and a callout on what to do when they get it 'wrong' — keep it silly, never correct the sound.

tools.title: Word stretch
tools.subtitle: Grow vocabulary from everyday moments

inputs.label: Where you are / what you're doing

tools.prompt: Turn the moment '{moment}' into a language-rich exchange for the profile child. Sections: a kv of 6 rich words to use naturally (Word → how to say it in context), a quote with a short model conversation (parent lines and likely child replies), bullets on expanding what the child says by one word, and a callout on avoiding quiz mode.
